assembly_instructions: Lay down the Basys-3-class black-composite PCB substrate with its four mounting holes, edge connector rows, USB/JTAG connector, power switch, oscillator, reset button, voltage regulator, 7-segment display, LEDs, and slide switches fixed to the board substrate.
Install the Artix-7 package base at the board center, then add the four low package rails as an open cutaway frame so the internal floorplan remains visible from isometric view.
Place the thin FPGA fabric floorplan plate on the exposed package base and root the accelerator blocks to that fabric plane.
Mount the single brass DSP48 K-RED multiplier at the center of the fabric and seat the copper highlight ring around its base to mark that exactly one DSP slice is active.

Attach the modular add unit on the forward coefficient path, the modular subtract unit on the inverse path, the op21 x1/2 halving gate directly after the subtract path, and the modular output mux before write-back.
Place the three small K-RED shift-add fold gates around the DSP48 multiplier and connect them as the multiplier-free modular-reduction chain that replaces the three Barrett multipliers.
Install the 1024x14 coefficient BRAM on one side of the DSP, add the dual-port BRAM arbiter beside it, then run separate copper read and write-back buses between the BRAM and the butterfly.
Install the half-height psi-fold twiddle ROM on the opposite side of the DSP, attach the psi-fold derive gate to the ROM, and run the twiddle bus into the DSP multiplier input.

Place the custom control FSM, BRAM address generator, ROM address driver, stage counter, mode register, and done flag along the rear edge of the fabric; connect control lines to BRAM, ROM, and datapath blocks in assembly order.

Add the timing pipeline strip and compact register bank above the butterfly datapath, connect them to the DSP48 and control FSM, and feed them from the board oscillator through the clock distribution spine.
Add the formal proof checker and formal obligation trace beside the controller, connect them to the done flag and datapath output, then bridge the verified done signal to the board LED bank.
Verify that every accelerator block is visible above the open package frame and that all non-root parts connect back through the fabric or board substrate.

info.summary: A formally-verified, DSP-minimal number-theoretic-transform accelerator for the Falcon/Proth prime q=12289 at N=1024, built around a single pipelined radix-2 butterfly that uses exactly one DSP48 slice on a small Artix-7 (Basys 3).
info.description: FoldNTT computes the length-1024 NTT modulo q=12289 in place on a single on-chip coefficient BRAM (1024x14, one RAMB18). Its lone pipelined radix-2 butterfly spends only ONE DSP48 slice because its K-RED modular multiplier replaces the reference design's three Barrett multipliers with shift-add 'folds', collapsing the multiply-reduce chain onto a single hardware multiplier. Twiddle factors are served from a psi-fold ROM that physically stores only half the words — a small shift-add gate derives the other half — so the twiddle table is a compact, half-height block.
info.description2: A small custom control FSM walks the transform, sequencing the BRAM address generator and the twiddle ROM. The datapath is coefficient BRAM -> K-RED butterfly (1 DSP multiply + modular add + modular sub + op21 x1/2 halving on the inverse path) -> written back in place. The op21 halving gate is the fix for a real bug found in the reference inverse transform. The whole core fits comfortably in an xc7a35t with a single DSP slice lit.

parts.name: Basys-3-class FPGA board substrate
parts.role: The scaled black PCB substrate carries the Artix-7 package and all Basys-3-style user I/O peripherals.

parts.name: Front-left mounting hole marker
parts.role: A plated mounting-hole marker fixes the PCB orientation and shows the board thickness at one corner.

parts.name: Front-right mounting hole marker
parts.role: A plated mounting-hole marker fixes the PCB orientation and shows the board thickness at the opposite front corner.

parts.name: Back-left mounting hole marker
parts.role: A plated mounting-hole marker identifies the rear-left corner of the dev board.

parts.name: Back-right mounting hole marker
parts.role: A plated mounting-hole marker identifies the rear-right corner of the dev board.

parts.name: Artix-7 package base
parts.role: The low package base supports the exposed xc7a35t floorplan without covering the accelerator blocks.

parts.name: Open package front rail
parts.role: The front rail is a cutaway package wall that frames the fabric while leaving the interior visible.

parts.name: Open package back rail
parts.role: The back rail is a cutaway package wall that frames the fabric while avoiding opaque coverage.

parts.name: Open package left rail
parts.role: The left rail defines the FPGA package edge and keeps the floorplan exposed in isometric view.

parts.name: Open package right rail
parts.role: The right rail defines the FPGA package edge and keeps all logic blocks visible above the package.

parts.name: Exposed FPGA fabric floorplan plate
parts.role: The thin fabric plate is the visible placement surface for the FoldNTT datapath and controller.

parts.name: K-RED DSP48 multiplier
parts.role: The central brass block is the single DSP48 slice used by the K-RED modular multiplier.

parts.name: Single-DSP highlight ring
parts.role: The copper ring encircles the one active DSP slice so the one-multiplier design choice is visually unambiguous.

parts.name: Modular add unit
parts.role: This butterfly unit computes the modular sum output for each radix-2 pair modulo q=12289.

parts.name: Modular subtract unit
parts.role: This butterfly unit computes the modular difference output before the optional inverse-path halving step.

parts.name: op21 x1/2 inverse halving gate
parts.role: The inverse-path gate applies the op21 one-half correction that fixes the reference inverse-transform bug.

parts.name: Butterfly output mux
parts.role: The output mux selects the add result and the inverse-corrected subtract result before both are written back to coefficient BRAM.

parts.name: K-RED shift-add fold gate 1
parts.role: This first fold gate performs a shift-add reduction step that replaces one Barrett multiplier stage.

parts.name: K-RED shift-add fold gate 2
parts.role: This second fold gate continues the K-RED shift-add reduction without consuming another DSP slice.

parts.name: K-RED shift-add fold gate 3
parts.role: This third fold gate completes the three-stage replacement for the removed Barrett multipliers.

parts.name: Coefficient BRAM 1024x14 RAMB18
parts.role: The single RAMB18 stores all 1024 fourteen-bit coefficients and is updated in place by the butterfly.

parts.name: BRAM dual-port read write arbiter
parts.role: The arbiter shows the shared RAMB18 port scheduling between coefficient reads and in-place write-back.

parts.name: Coefficient read bus
parts.role: This copper bus carries coefficient pairs from the RAMB18 into the central K-RED butterfly input.

parts.name: Coefficient write-back bus
parts.role: This separate copper bus returns the butterfly add/sub outputs to the same BRAM address space.

parts.name: Psi-fold twiddle ROM half-height
parts.role: The half-height ROM stores only half of the twiddle words for the N=1024 transform.

parts.name: Psi-fold derive gate
parts.role: The derive gate reconstructs the missing psi-fold twiddle half using shift-add logic beside the ROM.

parts.name: Twiddle factor bus
parts.role: This bus feeds selected twiddle factors from the psi-fold ROM into the DSP48 multiplier input.

parts.name: Custom control FSM
parts.role: The custom finite-state machine sequences all NTT stages, BRAM accesses, and twiddle selections.

parts.name: BRAM address generator
parts.role: The address generator emits the in-place read and write addresses for each butterfly pair.

parts.name: Twiddle ROM address driver
parts.role: The ROM address driver converts the current stage and butterfly index into a psi-fold ROM address.

parts.name: FSM control bus spine
parts.role: This thin control spine distributes FSM enables to the address generator, ROM driver, and datapath blocks.

parts.name: NTT stage counter
parts.role: The stage counter tracks the radix-2 transform stage across the 1024-point NTT schedule.

parts.name: Forward inverse mode register
parts.role: The mode register selects forward NTT or inverse NTT and enables the op21 halving path only when needed.

parts.name: Verified done flag latch
parts.role: The done flag latch represents the formally checked completion signal for the datapath controller.

parts.name: Radix-2 butterfly timing pipeline strip
parts.role: The narrow raised strip summarizes the registered pipeline stages that carry each coefficient pair through the single radix-2 butterfly.

parts.name: Compact butterfly register bank
parts.role: The compact register bank makes the cycle-aligned butterfly pipeline visible without modeling every flip-flop as a separate part.

params.reason: cycle alignment for coefficient pair, twiddle, add/sub, and write-back

parts.name: Formal datapath proof checker
parts.role: The proof checker block marks the formally verified equivalence and completion checks that watch the controller and write-back datapath.

parts.name: Formal obligation trace
parts.role: This trace ties the proof checker to the controller, done latch, and write-back path so verification is shown as a connected observation path.

parts.name: Clock distribution spine
parts.role: The clock spine carries the board oscillator clock into the controller and registered butterfly pipeline.

parts.name: Verified status LED bridge
parts.role: This routed status bridge carries the verified done signal from the FPGA core to the board LED bank.

parts.name: USB JTAG connector
parts.role: The USB/JTAG connector programs the Artix-7 and powers the board during development.

parts.name: Board power switch
parts.role: The slide power switch controls board power before the FPGA configuration loads.

parts.name: Top PMOD expansion header
parts.role: The top PMOD row anchors the board as a Basys-3-style teaching FPGA platform.

parts.name: Right PMOD expansion header
parts.role: The right PMOD row shows the additional expansion edge used on small FPGA dev boards.

parts.name: Four-digit seven-segment display
parts.role: The four-digit display provides visible status output for test firmware and transform completion.

parts.name: Slide switch bank
parts.role: The grouped slide-switch bank represents user inputs such as mode select and reset options.

parts.name: User LED bank
parts.role: The LED bank exposes simple debug bits from the controller and done flag during bring-up.

parts.name: Board clock oscillator
parts.role: The oscillator supplies the board clock used by the synchronous NTT controller and datapath.

parts.name: Reset push button
parts.role: The push button provides a manual reset input to the control FSM during board tests.

parts.name: FPGA voltage regulator
parts.role: The regulator block represents the board power stage feeding the Artix-7 package rails.

parts.name: VGA display connector
parts.role: The VGA connector is a recognizable Basys-3 board peripheral outside the FoldNTT core.
